This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER Case diary is available.
This is seventh application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 28.07.2021 in connection with Crime No.309/2021 registered at Police Station Hazira, District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

The first and fourth applications of applicant were dismissed on merits vide orders dated 12.11.2021 Sonu Prajapati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15299213/
1 and 06.09.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. Nos.50399/2021 and 41971/2022 respectively.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The third bail application (MCRC No.23325/2022) of applicant was dismissed due to non-compliance of peremptory order dated 14.06.2022.

The applicant's second, fifth and sixth bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn by orders dated 04.01.2022, 06.12.2022 and 08.02.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.
Nos.60829/2021, 55014/2022 and 6417/2023 respectively.
Prosecution story, in brief, is that applicant kidnapped/abducted the minor prosecutrix and kept her in captivity for a long period and committed rape on her.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the sixth bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 08.02.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.6417/2023 with liberty to file afresh in the week commencing 12th June, 2023 on the ground of delay in trial if the trial is not concluded by that time.
As statements of prosecutrix along-with other witnesses are yet to be recorded and trial will still take time to conclude, therefore, this seventh bail application has been preferred.
He further submits that prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
She in her statement recorded during investigation under Section 164 of Cr.P.C has specifically stated that she went with the applicant and stayed with him voluntarily.
The DNA test report does not support the prosecution case.

The applicant is in custody since 28.07.2021 and the trial will take time to conclude, therefore,
in the aforesaid circumstances, applicant is entitled for grant of bail.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident and no circumstantial change is there after the rejection of sixth bail application.
Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

Having considered rival submissions, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant,
statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C and specially the period of custody,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Aman Sonu Prajapati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15299213/
